stem:
Fig. 8.1 shows part of the emission spectrum of visible radiation emitted by hydrogen gas in a star in a distant galaxy.

[[fig:f1]]

The galaxy is moving away from the Earth at a speed of 6.2 × 10⁶ m s⁻¹.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.text: Explain how the positions of the lines in the emission spectrum seen by an observer on the Earth differ from the positions shown in Fig. 8.1.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: On Fig. 8.1, draw the three lines in possible positions in the spectrum seen by the observer.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead: The lines in Fig. 8.1 correspond to electron transitions down to the energy level −3.40 eV. One of the lines represents emitted radiation of wavelength 488 nm.
parts.text: Calculate the energy of a photon of this radiation.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the energy, in eV, of the energy level from which the electron transition originates to cause the emission of this radiation.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the wavelength, in nm, of this radiation as detected by the observer on the Earth.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
A value for the Hubble constant is 2.3 × 10⁻¹⁸ s⁻¹.

Determine the distance of the galaxy from the Earth.

figures.caption: Fig. 8.1
figures.alt: A horizontal spectrum with three vertical emission lines and an arrow indicating increasing frequency to the right.
